subject: Transportation Systems
title: Airlines Take Over
description: A 60-second lesson on Airlines Take Over.

hook.text: In the 1950s, jet airliners crossed the Atlantic in eight hours. Ocean liners took five days.

buildup.text: For long distances, planes were faster and often cheaper. Rail lost its cross-country advantage.

discovery.text: By the 1970s, nobody took a train from New York to Chicago when a flight took just two hours.

twist.text: Airlines couldn't kill short-distance rail. Most commuters still ride trains—just not far.

climax.text: Today, trains and planes compete on routes under 500 miles, where airport hassle erases speed gains.

punchline.text: Planes won the long haul. Trains kept the short one.

quiz.question: On what routes do trains still compete with airlines?
